transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my technology review. I tested the draft online ballot this morning and confirmed that the platform records each voter's identity for 90 days, and there is no way to disable that record. This creates a significant privacy concern for our student voters. The approved workaround for this issue is to use sealed paper ballots counted by two adults, with zero electronic voter records. I have not yet updated the election plan to reflect this finding, but it clearly needs to be incorporated before Dr. Morgan approves the plan.

transcript.text: I need to share a critical concern from my confidential student-safety review. I identified a substantiated retaliation concern involving two students who are participating in the election. Because of this, our student-privacy protocol requires anonymous voting and prohibits releasing vote totals until the election is certified. I've kept the details of this review in my counseling file because it contains protected student information, and I have not yet briefed Dr. Morgan on this. This means the draft plan's current provision to publish vote totals at the end of election day must be changed — vote totals cannot be released until the election is officially certified. Anonymous voting is also essential, which aligns with Mr. Shah's recommendation for sealed paper ballots with no electronic voter records.

I confirmed with families that election instructions, ballots, and candidate statements are needed in English, Spanish, and Arabic. The translation request is still pending with the communications office, but the draft plan currently lists only English. This needs to be incorporated into the plan before Dr. Morgan approves it — we must ensure all three languages are provided so that all families can fully participate in and understand the election process.

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Ellis and Ms. Romero, for sharing those important findings. It's clear that all three of our concerns actually align and reinforce each other. Ms. Ellis, your requirement for anonymous voting is perfectly consistent with the sealed paper ballot workaround I identified — paper ballots with no electronic voter records will ensure student anonymity. And Ms. Romero, your translation requirement will need to be incorporated into the revised plan as well, since the candidate statements and ballot instructions will now be on paper rather than online. I'd recommend that I update the draft election plan to reflect all three findings: the switch to sealed paper ballots counted by two adults, the delay of vote total publication until certification, and the inclusion of English, Spanish, and Arabic translations for all election materials.
